A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same K-Merge research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-merging experiments across 40 tasks with two language models, together with ordering, threshold, clustering, efficiency, and generalization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds similarity and weighting ablations in Tables 3-4 and Llama-3.2-3B results in Table A.7.

M1.justification: The cosine-based assignment, history-weighted averaging, threshold rule, and inference mapping remain unchanged in Equations 5-9 and Algorithm 1. Section 3.3 clarifies task identification without establishing a newly implemented routing component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five problem types across eight languages and the same held-out translation and title-generation tasks in Portuguese, Turkish, and Serbian. The additional model and component ablations do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The principal comparator set is retained. New Table 4 additionally evaluates history-aware versions of TIES, DARE, and DARE-TIES against their constant-weight versions; history-aware Linear already corresponds to K-Merge.

E3.justification: Existing splits, training settings, metrics, and benchmark protocols remain unchanged. Added experiments vary similarity measures at K=3 and 5, weighting schemes at K=1 and 3, and evaluate Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct at K=1, 3, 5, and 7.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused ablations comparing cosine similarity with L1, L2, and L-infinity measures and history-aware with constant merging weights (Tables 3-4). Existing ordering robustness, threshold sensitivity, clustering, and cross-task generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: New Tables 3, 4, and A.7 explicitly report single-seed experiments without uncertainty estimates. The original three-ordering averages and standard deviations remain unchanged in v1 Tables A.5-A.6, renumbered A.4-A.5 in v2; no reduction in those original repetitions is established.

E6.justification: Existing results are retained. New Table 3 reports K-Merge scoring 0.75 with cosine versus 0.66 with each alternative measure at K=3; Table 4 adds weighting comparisons. New 3B results include K-Merge beating Linear 0.82 versus 0.81 at K=7 and tying at 0.77 at K=5. These are additional experiments, not revised v1 scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, aggregate-score definition, and Equations 1-9 are unchanged, with no added proofs or theorems. Section 3.3 explains the known-task premise already used by Equation 3 and the inference procedure.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about storage-constrained continual merging, lightweight data-free methods, performance, and K-Merge++ ordering robustness. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New Section 3.3 explicitly excludes routing errors through an ideal task-classification assumption. Added discussions support cosine selection, explain K-Merge as history-aware Linear merging, and extend the performance interpretation to 3B models. The existing limitations and ethical considerations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 expands the English-only prompt table into language-specific listings in Table A.8 and attributes them to Ceritli et al. It also adds a project-page link. These are documentation and access-pointer additions; the PDFs do not establish changed underlying multilingual prompts or newly available code.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bohdal et al. (2026) on data-driven adapter clustering and merging and Sokar et al. (2025) on aligned continual model merging. The central research positioning is retained; most other reference changes concern bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 adds the task-identification subsection and short experimental discussions, reorders the appendix's clustering and threshold subsections, and updates affiliation wording and bibliography presentation. The main narrative and method exposition remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3, 4, and A.7 and expands and relocates the prompt table into full-page Table A.8. Existing figures are retained with layout shifts and table renumbering. Some Chinese prompt text in the new table is visibly incomplete in both checked renderings.

improvement.justification: The added component ablations and 3B evaluation provide useful supporting evidence, while Section 3.3 clarifies the routing assumption and Table A.8 improves prompt documentation. The gains are limited by single-seed reporting for the new experiments and incomplete Chinese prompt text. These additions improve support and transparency without substantially changing the paper's scientific scope.
